message: SP-12 — Question on the widget contract. Do I read from c.data directly in the template or copy it off at bootstrap?
SP-12 — Copy it off at bootstrap into c.entries and c.allowedShifts. Every write re-runs the whole server script and returns fresh data, so you patch your local maps rather than reloading the page.
SP-12 — Got it. So the template only ever renders c. That keeps the refresh path clean.
SP-13 — All custom classes are namespaced shift- now. Bootstrap 3 and Font Awesome are already there from Service Portal so I am not shipping either.

SP-20 — Warning for everyone touching date code. Client, data.month and input.month are 0-indexed. The stored month column is 1-indexed. Conversion happens at the table boundary and nowhere else.
SP-20 — That has bitten me twice already this week. Can we put it at the top of the README so it is not tribal knowledge.
SP-72 — Yes. Calling it the number one footgun in the doc so nobody discovers it in production.

SP-39 — Strong yes. The alternative is string comparison against display names, and the first time someone renames a type in production we get a silent pay bug.

SP-18 — Correct, those need the per-day entitlement transaction. I am adding a blocksBulk guard that rejects them server-side. Do not rely on hiding them in the dropdown, the server call is reachable from the browser with any payload.
SP-18 — Understood. Client filtering is convenience, the server decides.
SP-41 — Good call. A background script inherits whatever scope the session happens to be in, and that has consequences that take an hour to clean up.
SP-42 — Added validateCatalogue. If an active row has no day_category, or CO is enabled with no consuming type, the widget shows a config banner instead of behaving unpredictably.
SP-57 — The client branches on an error field on the response. Checking whether the server ever sets it.
SP-57 — It does not. All six refusal paths use addErrorMessage, which never reaches the widget response. So the check is dead code on both sides.
Taking SP-32 and SP-34 together. Both are mine end to end so the extraction lands in one piece rather than half a refactor.

SP-32 — Context for why this matters. The aggregation is currently inline in the calendar and hard-wired to the session user. The manager widget has to aggregate a reportee, so as it stands it cannot reuse a line of it.
SP-32 — Extract it. Do not let anyone write a second copy for the manager side. A second copy of payroll maths that drifts is a pay bug with a delayed fuse.
SP-32 — Agreed and I will put that in the file header so it survives me.

SP-35 — The entitlement ordering is trickier than the BRD makes it sound. The decision about which entitlement a CO consumes has to be made before the day row exists, but recorded after it is written.
SP-35 — So it is a three-phase thing. Release the previous state, write the day, commit the new state, with the reservation in between.
SP-35 — Exactly that. releasePrevious, write, commitForNew, with reserveForNew claiming what the CO needs. Any other order either loses an entitlement or grants one twice.

SP-64 — Deployment trap worth broadcasting. The CLI get verb ignores the sys_id parameter. It silently returns the first row of the whole table. I verified a widget push against a completely different record for twenty minutes.
SP-64 — That is a nasty one because the readback looks like it passed. Always query by sys_id in the encoded query then.
SP-64 — Yes. Adding it to the deployment notes with the other three traps.

SP-65 — And another. Create is not idempotent and nothing warns you. I now have two active Script Includes sharing one API name, created eleven seconds apart. The platform resolves that unpredictably.
SP-65 — How do you delete one? Is there a delete verb?

SP-65 — There is not. It tells you to use the UI. And the confirmation dialog renders inside the main iframe, so an automated click in the top frame finds nothing and silently leaves the record alive.
SP-62 — Please write all of this down. This is the kind of thing that costs the next person a full day.

SP-63 — Wrote a deploy helper. It builds an ASCII-escaped, newline-normalised body file and refuses to emit one that does not round-trip. A push can return HTTP 200 and store garbage, so it also prints the readback command.
SP-63 — This has already saved me. My template had a non-ASCII character in a comment and the old path stored it mangled.
SP-33 — Question on the aggregator. Should recompute update the existing summary rows or replace them?
SP-33 — Replace. Delete then insert per shift type for the affected month and weeks. Incrementing drifts the moment one write fails halfway, and there is no cheap way to detect that it has.
SP-33 — One known wart then. The rate map reads active catalogue rows only, so a type deactivated after being logged re-aggregates at zero.
SP-33 — Leave it for now and document it. The extraction should be behaviour-neutral, so fixing it in the same change makes the refactor unreviewable. Log it separately.

SP-37 — Third Script Include going in. Calendar rules owns the catalogue read, the holiday set, the weekend classification and the composed allowed-shift list.
SP-38 — Do I construct entitlements alongside it in the manager widget or does rules give me one?

SP-38 — Rules builds and owns it. Ask it for the instance. If you construct one alongside, the catalogue gets read twice and the two copies can disagree about semantics, which is the worst possible failure mode here.
SP-51 — Appreciated. Ping me before you pin a selector to a class I might rename and I will keep it stable.
SP-24 — Design question on bulk approve. Should I issue one bulk query or loop the single-row action?
SP-24 — Loop the single-row action. A bulk query bypasses every authorisation and state guard exactly once and nobody notices until it matters. It is slower and correct.
SP-25 — Then the single-row action needs to return its refusal rather than throw, so the bulk path can collect reasons into one summary.
SP-57 — Yes, and note that the manager widget is now the widget that gets error reporting right. The calendar still does not.
SP-23 — Good catch. Deriving the selection from the visible rows only, not the full set.
SP-27 — Starting manager day correction. This one needs care: it lets a manager change someone else's logged day.
SP-28 — So the new shift goes through the same allowed check as the employee, evaluated for that reportee not for the manager. Plus a reportee assertion before anything is touched.
SP-27 — Correction runs the same three-phase entitlement transaction as the calendar. It has to, otherwise correcting a day that granted a CO leaves the entitlement dangling.

SP-59 — The manager lead stat tile. Bind it to the all count instead of the submitted count. It is display-only, no write path reads those counts, so it cannot touch data.
SP-60 — Found something while writing the holiday case. The system property the holiday lookup reads does not exist. No property in that namespace exists at all.
SP-60 — Since the beginning. The lookup returns an empty set and every date classifies as a weekday or weekend. Recording it as TC-SP-030. Not automating it because it produces no screenshot.
SP-61 — Related, TC-SP-031. The five default table names in the calendar server script name no table that exists. The widget only runs because the portal instance overrides all five.
Raised SP-60 and SP-61. Both go on the board as documented findings even though neither is automated. A finding that only lives in Slack is a finding we lose.

SP-31 — Working on hiding pay amounts for managers without the permission. Should I hide them in the template?

SP-31 — No. Strip them from the data server-side. A guard that lives only in the template is not a guard, the server call is reachable from the browser with any payload and the response is right there in the network tab.
